draft.title: Commas and brackets
card: List
Commas separate items in a list: Mia packed a hat, a drink bottle and a towel. The comma before "and" is usually left out in Australian school writing.
Introductory clause
A comma follows an opening clause that comes before the main clause: When the bell rang, the students left. The main clause is the part that could stand alone as a sentence.
Extra information
A pair of commas can mark off extra information in the middle of a sentence: Mr Lee, our coach, was late. Take the extra part out and the sentence still makes sense.
Brackets
Brackets also hold extra information the sentence could do without: The match (which was postponed twice) finally began. Brackets always come in pairs.
draft.remember: Commas separate, follow openers and mark off extras. Brackets hold extras the sentence can do without.

opts: Jess bought apples, pears and plums
Jess bought, apples pears and plums
Jess, bought apples pears, and plums
Jess bought apples pears, and, plums
a.why: A comma goes between each item in a list, and "and" joins the last two. The other options put commas in the middle of a item group or after the verb, where they do not separate items.
a.clue: Which one puts a comma between the items, not before them?

b.q: Which sentence punctuates the extra information correctly?
opts: Our dog Biscuit, a kelpie, loves the beach
Our dog Biscuit, a kelpie loves the beach
Our dog Biscuit a kelpie, loves the beach
Our dog, Biscuit a kelpie, loves the beach
b.why: The extra information "a kelpie" needs a comma before and after it, so the pair marks it off. The other options use only one comma or put the commas in the wrong places, so the extra part is not properly marked off.
b.clue: Extra information needs a comma on both sides.

a.best: Jess bought apples, pears and plums

b.best: Our dog Biscuit, a kelpie, loves the beach

problems.detail: Why (a) has a grammar slip and is unclear: "in the middle of a item group" should be "an item", and "item group" is a confusing phrase. It also says the wrong options put commas "after the verb", but one of them puts the comma after the subject ("Jess, bought"), not after the verb.
